players.product: air-treatment & evaporative cooling systems for data centers

quarterly_data.signal: Exceptional Q2 demand: organic order intake up more than 140%, order backlog up 151%, group book-to-bill an impressive 2.3 times; net sales +6% (organically a little more). Americas generated 76% of order intake (EMEA a little shy of 20%, APAC shy of 10%). AirTech also exceptional with book-to-bill of 1.7 and a second consecutive quarter of SEK 2 billion-plus underlying order intake (components/evaporative pads surged on competitors' delivery problems — market share gains, some deliveries scheduled into 2027). Strong cash flow driven by customer advances in Data Center Technologies; group price increases of 2.8% in the quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: Organic order intake +more than 140%; backlog +151%; book-to-bill 2.3; net sales +6%; group price increases 2.8%

quarterly_data.signal: Data Center Technologies book-to-bill of 3.6 — 'super confident in the order backlog'; no signs of any slowdown in demand, orders cutting across all product categories. One significant order of SEK 2 billion announced at the beginning of the quarter, plus an EMEA co-located order across CDUs. Deliveries are mainly for 2026 and 2027 but Munters is 'also starting to fill up 2028'. DCT net sales declined as expected on the planned US chiller production ramp-up, worsened by supply chain constraints — without them net sales would have been about SEK 300 million higher in the quarter. Setting up DCT for accelerated revenue growth starting Q3, accelerating in Q4, carrying through 2027 and 2028.
quarterly_data.figure: DCT book-to-bill 3.6; SEK 2 billion order booked; deliveries filling 2026, 2027 and starting 2028; ~SEK 300 million net sales held back by supply constraints

quarterly_data.signal: Supply chain constraints are the bottleneck, not demand: market-wide crunch in FANS plus valves and certain components; the setup of a localized US bill of material was delayed, forcing continued shipment of components from Europe into the US — tariff impact in the quarter was 3% (imports of finished goods from Italian production and chiller components from Europe). Ramp-up is about ONE QUARTER BEHIND plan. Factory build itself is on track: Virginia facility production output DOUBLED and floor space increased 60%. Mitigation: qualifying new fan suppliers, pre-ordering/building stock, organizing supply outside North America; no delivery delays to customers expected (product-mix shifts across the wide portfolio), no signs of customer dissatisfaction or share loss to competitors.
quarterly_data.figure: Tariff impact 3%; ramp one quarter behind plan; Virginia output doubled, floor space +60%

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 outlook unchanged: DCT full-year sales growth guidance of 30% still valid ('I use the frame 30%-40%, for sure, 30%') but tilted toward the end of the year — gradual output increase in Q3, 'the real revenue booster will come in Q4' (implying more than SEK 3 billion in the final quarter, feasible with all capacity and people installed). Adjusted EBITA margin expected to improve during H2 on DCT backlog conversion and step-by-step AirTech improvement (AirTech cost programs: 2025 completed above plan, 2026 delivered over SEK 100 million so far, at least SEK 250 million by year-end; AirTech target range 13%). Midterm: DCT margins should reach the HIGH TEENS once supply chain is worked through; group target 14% over a business cycle; future Munters (ex-FoodTech, being positioned for divestment) seen delivering annual revenues well above SEK 20 billion in coming years (vs SEK 6.5 billion seven years ago).
quarterly_data.figure: DCT FY sales growth guidance 30% unchanged (tilted to Q4); AirTech savings at least SEK 250 million in 2026; revenue ambition above SEK 20 billion ex-FoodTech
